title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Tech Wipeout Rolls In on an Amazon and Intel Undertow
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures are down more than 2 percent after disappointing results from Amazon and Intel revived worries about Big Tech's AI spending. Oil is up again while gold and bitcoin slip.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are down about 1.0% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 2.3% in early trading.
Dow futures are roughly flat and Russell 2000 futures are down about 0.6%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.99%, slightly lower, and the dollar is tracking yields lower.
WTI crude is up about 2% to around $104 on Iran conflict worries; gold is down under 1% near $4,000.
Bitcoin is down about 3.4% near $77,000, and the VIX is up to about 18.3.
Asia: the Bank of Japan held rates at 1.25%, raised its inflation forecast and signaled more hikes ahead; the yen is near 157 per dollar.
Europe: equity futures are mixed.
Early pre-market quotes; levels can shift before the open.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: Employment Cost Index for Q3, expected +0.8% after +0.9% last quarter.
8:45 AM CT: Chicago PMI for October, expected 54.6 after 58.8.
The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with two dissents favoring a hike; next meeting is December 8-9.
Thursday's data were hot: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualized, September core PCE rose 0.3% for 3.1% year over year, and jobless claims fell to 194,000.
Main story: renewed worries about Big Tech's AI spending, plus sticky inflation and high oil.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Amazon missed earnings expectations despite faster cloud growth; shares are down around 7% pre-market.
Intel beat third-quarter estimates but gave a weak fourth-quarter outlook on soft PC sales; shares are sharply lower pre-market.
Alphabet fell about 12% Thursday after a big earnings miss and heavy cash burn, its worst day in years.
ServiceNow fell about 27% Thursday on softer growth guidance; Fortinet fell about 20% after trimming its service revenue outlook.
Before the open today: ExxonMobil, Chevron, AbbVie, AstraZeneca, BP, Sanofi and General Dynamics.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: AMZN (Amazon): about -7% — rare earnings miss and AI spending worries, even as cloud sales growth sped up to 39%.
INTC (Intel): sharply lower — weak fourth-quarter outlook on sluggish PC sales overshadowed a quarterly beat.
GOOGL (Alphabet): extending losses after Thursday's roughly 12% drop on an earnings miss.
NOW (ServiceNow): after a 27% drop Thursday on slower remaining-performance-obligation guidance.
FTNT (Fortinet): after a 20% drop Thursday on a cut to its service revenue outlook.
SNDK (Sandisk): in focus after solid results and an 8-for-1 stock split.
RDDT (Reddit): in focus after saying it will limit logged-out access to the site.

sections.title: Business News
items: Amazon and Alphabet results reignited worries about how much Big Tech is spending on AI.
Oil is heading for a big monthly gain, with Brent up about 12% in October on the Iran conflict.
Microsoft drew strong demand for a $25 billion bond sale to fund AI buildout.
The Bank of Japan held steady but leaned toward more rate hikes.
Eli Lilly raised its 2026 sales forecast on strong demand, and FedEx raised its profit outlook.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT Employment Cost Index — a hot wage reading would add to inflation worries after Thursday's data.
Big oil earnings from ExxonMobil and Chevron with crude above $100.
Whether tech selling spreads at the open, with the VIX near 18 and month-end trading today.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, October thirtieth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding the board with me is Gus the wonder dog, and he's been staring at the waves since sunrise. Give the Dawn Patrol a howdy, Gus! Alright, conditions this morning are poor, with a tech wipeout rolling in. First, the swell. S and P five hundred futures are down about one percent. Nasdaq one hundred futures are down about two point three percent. Dow futures are roughly flat, and Russell two thousand futures are off about half a percent. These are early quotes, so things can shift. The ten year Treasury yield is near four point nine nine percent, a touch lower. Crude oil is up about two percent to around one hundred four dollars a barrel. Gold slips under one percent, bitcoin drops more than three percent, and the VIX fear gauge climbs to about eighteen. Overseas, the Bank of Japan held rates steady but hinted at more hikes, and Europe looks mixed. Now the wind and weather. At seven thirty A M Central, we get the employment cost index, expected up point eight percent. At eight forty five A M Central, it's the Chicago P M I, expected at fifty four point six. The Fed held rates on Wednesday, but two members wanted a hike. And Thursday's data ran hot, with growth at three point four percent and core inflation at three point one percent. On to the tide chart. Amazon missed earnings, and the stock is down around seven percent before the bell, even though cloud sales sped up. Intel beat on the quarter but gave a soft outlook, and that stock is taking a gnarly drop early. Alphabet already wiped out yesterday, down about twelve percent. ServiceNow and Fortinet got tossed hard too. The big worry is how much Big Tech is spending on A I. Before the open today, we hear from ExxonMobil, Chevron, AbbVie and AstraZeneca. In the lineup, Sandisk posted solid results and an eight for one stock split, so that grommet of a chip stock is catching a nice little wave. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Reddit is also in the news after saying it will limit access for logged out users. On the beach, oil is headed for a big monthly gain on the Iran conflict, and Microsoft sold a huge twenty five billion dollar bond to fund its A I buildout. Sets to watch today: that wage report at seven thirty, the big oil earnings, and whether tech selling spreads at the open on this last trading day of the month. Soul surfers, don't let one gnarly set knock you off your board. Want my call on a particular wave? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
